title: Phase identity for normalized cube blocks
statement:
Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $a,b:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb R$, and let $x,y$ be Boolean vectors of length $nm$. Then
\[
\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigl(a_i A_i(x)+b_i A_i(y)\bigr)
=
\sum_{k=0}^{nm-1}\left(\frac{a_{i(k)}}{\sqrt m}\sigma(x_k)+\frac{b_{i(k)}}{\sqrt m}\sigma(y_k)\right),
\]
where $A_i(z)$ is the sum of the signs of the entries in block $i$, divided by $\sqrt m$, and $i(k)$ is the block index of coordinate $k$ under the standard identification of coordinates with pairs in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\times\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Here $\sigma$ sends Boolean values to their signs, with false mapped to $1$ and true to $-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $a,b$ are real-valued functions on the $n$ coordinates
